answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the kernel identifier and voids the later submissions, and thus the operator burns for 166 runs and collects one. Because the forge index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the delta audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 166 answers need 166 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
